🏍️ Why Is KTM Failing? | The Untold Story of KTM's Downfall in India 🇮🇳

Once the dream bike of every young Indian rider, KTM is now struggling to maintain its position in the Indian motorcycle market. What went wrong? How did a brand that revolutionized the entry-level sports bike segment with KTM Duke 200, RC 390, and its aggressive image lose its dominance?

In this deep-dive case study, we uncover the real story behind KTM’s downfall in India.

From its early success to today’s sales decline, this video breaks down:

Poor after-sales service

Rising competition from Royal Enfield, Yamaha, and TVS

The saturation of the street-racer segment

KTM’s pricing strategy becoming a liability

And how Bajaj’s partnership both helped and hurt the brand in the long run

We’ll also explore whether KTM’s aggressive branding and loud street presence is no longer appealing to Indian bikers, who are now shifting towards more refined, touring-friendly motorcycles.

🔍 What You’ll Learn in This Video:
✅ The complete history and rise of KTM in India
✅ How KTM’s bold marketing and edgy design initially won hearts
✅ Reasons why KTM sales are dropping sharply post-2020
✅ The impact of Bajaj-KTM joint venture on production and branding
✅ KTM vs Royal Enfield – who’s winning the new-age biker battle?
✅ Can KTM make a comeback with upcoming models and electric bikes?

📊 Data-Backed Analysis
We’ll look at:

Year-on-year KTM sales data in India

Market share comparisons with Royal Enfield, Yamaha R15, and TVS Apache

Shift in customer mindset post-2022

Why even KTM lovers are now choosing alternatives
